task.title: A set of functions for grades and prices
task.description: Write functions that return their result with return and print nothing: isEven(number) - a function declaration, true for an even number; getGrade(score) - 5 for 90 and above, 4 from 75, 3 from 60, otherwise 2; formatPrice(amount, currency) - the string "45000 UZS", currency defaults to "UZS"; square - an arrow function in a constant, the square of a number; countVowels(word) - the number of vowels a, e, i, o, u ignoring case. You may print test calls after the functions.

tests.name: isEven: 4 and 0 are even, 7 is not
tests.check: isEven(4) === true && isEven(0) === true && isEven(7) === false
tests.fail: return number % 2 === 0; - a comparison already gives true or false.

tests.name: isEven works with negatives: -3 is odd, -8 is even
tests.fail: -3 % 2 is -1, not 1. Check the remainder against 0: number % 2 === 0.

tests.name: getGrade: 75 → 4, 74 → 3, 60 → 3, 59 → 2, 0 → 2
tests.fail: Check the >= 75 and >= 60 boundaries and that the grade is a number.

tests.name: formatPrice(20, "$") → "20 $"
tests.fail: Use the currency parameter in the template string.

tests.name: currency defaults to "UZS"
tests.fail: Set the value in the parameter list: currency = "UZS".

tests.name: square is an arrow function in a constant
tests.fail: Write it with an arrow: const square = (x) => ...;

tests.name: countVowels: "JavaScript" → 3, "EDUCATION" → 5, "rhythm" → 0, "" → 0
tests.fail: A counter inside the function, for...of over word, char.toLowerCase(), return count.

tests.name: The functions return results instead of printing
tests.check: (() => { const before = __logs.length; isEven(2); getGrade(80); formatPrice(1); square(2); countVowels("ab"); return __logs.length === before; })()
tests.fail: Remove console.log from the function bodies - the result is given back with return.

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: There is an error in the code - read its text in the console.

hints: A function returns a result: return ...; Without return the call gives undefined.
Even: number % 2 === 0 - works for negatives too.
An early exit is handy in getGrade: if (score >= 90) { return 5; }
Declare the vowel counter inside the function, otherwise the second call continues the old count.

questions.question: What does this print: function hi() { console.log("Hello"); } hi;
options: Nothing: the function is not called
questions.explanation: A call always has parentheses: hi().

questions.question: In function greet(name) { ... } greet("Anna"); match the terms.
questions.explanation: A parameter is a name in the declaration, an argument is a value in the call.

questions.question: What does this print: function f(x) { console.log(x * 2); } const r = f(5); console.log(r);
questions.explanation: f prints 10 but returns nothing - r is undefined.

questions.question: Which keyword returns a result from a function? Type it.
questions.explanation: return value; - the result of the call.

questions.question: What does getCost(150000) return? function getCost(t) { if (t >= 100000) { return 0; } return 15000; }
questions.explanation: After return the function ends, the second line does not run.

questions.question: What does this print: function price(a, c = "UZS") { return `${a} ${c}`; } console.log(price(500));
questions.explanation: No argument passed - the default value is used.

questions.question: Which are valid arrow functions returning a doubled number?
questions.explanation: With curly braces an explicit return is needed. Parentheses around a single parameter can be omitted.

questions.question: What does this print: function calc() { const result = 42; } calc(); console.log(result);
questions.explanation: A variable inside a function is not visible outside.

questions.question: Which function is pure?
options: function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
questions.explanation: The result depends only on the arguments, nothing outside changes.

questions.question: Which function names follow the course style?
questions.explanation: A function is an action: a verb or an is/has/can question. total is a name for a value.

questions.question: What does square(-4) return if const square = (x) => x * x;? Type the number.
Match the task with the tool.
pairs: Give a result to the program
Show a value to a person
Use a value if no argument is passed
questions.explanation: return is for the program, console.log is for debugging.
